## Optimize the Remaining Motion

A backward Riccati recursion minimizes a stage cost **plus the optimal remaining cost**. Repeatedly choosing the cheapest current action is a different, generally greedy procedure. For linear dynamics $\delta x_{k+1}=A_k\delta x_k+B_k\delta u_k$, use

$$
\begin{aligned}
J&=\frac12\delta x_N^\top Q_N\delta x_N+\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\ell_k,\\
\ell_k&=\frac12(\delta x_k^\top Q_k\delta x_k+\delta u_k^\top R_k\delta u_k).
\end{aligned}
$$

where $Q_k,Q_N\succeq0$, $R_k\succ0$, and no state/input constraints are imposed. The state has dimension $n$ and input dimension $m$; the weights must match their units or declared scaling.

## Complete the Bellman Square

Set $S_N=Q_N$. The quadratic in $\delta u_k$ has positive definite Hessian $H_k=R_k+B_k^\top S_{k+1}B_k$. Minimization gives

$$
K_k=H_k^{-1}B_k^\top S_{k+1}A_k,\qquad \delta u_k=-K_k\delta x_k,
$$

$$
S_k=Q_k+A_k^\top S_{k+1}A_k-K_k^\top H_kK_k.
$$

Induction gives $S_k\succeq0$ and invertible $H_k$. Solve the linear system numerically instead of forming an explicit inverse. This is the exact global optimum of the stated linear-quadratic problem. It is a local model of a nonlinear problem, and its value matrix need not be positive definite.

## DDP Uses More Than This Recursion

For nonlinear transition $F$ and stage cost $\ell$, expand $\mathcal Q(x,u)=\ell(x,u)+V^+(F(x,u))$. Its second derivatives contain both $F_a^\top V^+_{xx}F_b$ and $\sum_i(V_x^+)_iD^2_{ab}F_i$, for $a,b\in\{x,u\}$. Full DDP keeps the latter dynamics-curvature terms; iLQR commonly drops them. Linear cost terms, mixed derivatives and a feedforward update also matter [@tassa2014control].

When $\mathcal Q_{uu}\succ0$, the unconstrained local step is $\delta u=-\mathcal Q_{uu}^{-1}\mathcal Q_u-\mathcal Q_{uu}^{-1}\mathcal Q_{ux}\delta x$. A nonlinear forward rollout and line search test improvement. Regularization changes the step; control bounds require a constrained subproblem. None of these algorithmic operations alone certifies contraction.

## Scope and Limitations

**Finite-horizon LQR does not require controllability.** With $Q,Q_N\succeq0$ and $R\succ0$, the recursion remains well defined even for $B=0$. The continuous scalar problem $\dot x=x$, $B=0$, $Q=1$, zero terminal cost has $S(t)=(e^{2(T-t)}-1)/2$, finite on every finite horizon. Infinite-horizon stabilization is a separate question: stabilizability and detectability are standard sufficient assumptions for the time-invariant stabilizing solution. A hard endpoint constraint can be infeasible despite a well-posed unconstrained problem.

**Cost is not automatically energy.** Squared torque, mechanical work, impact accuracy and tissue loading measure different things. A modeled optimum does not establish a human neural objective or clinical safety. Report weight sensitivity, actuator feasibility and the evidence behind the underlying mechanics.
